args.task: Search for news from 2026 regarding Julie Won's positions, statements, or legislative progress on housing promises (Comprehensive Planning, NYCHA funding, housing discrimination task force, zoning for arts spaces).

result:
* On October 10, 2023, Council Member Julie Won announced the launch of holistic community planning processes in District 26, including the *One Long Island City* study and planning corridors for Astoria, Sunnyside, and Woodside ([nyc.gov](https://council.nyc.gov/julie-won/2023/10/10/council-member-julie-won-announces-comprehensive-community-planning-for-district-26/)).
* In a November 5, 2026 podcast interview, Council Member Won highlighted that she approved over 15,000 units of housing under major rezonings in her district during her tenure ([youtube.com](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V6zn6Q9-EwU)).
* On June 30, 2026, following the adoption of the city budget, Council Member Won announced that the City Council secured funding for NYCHA and affordable housing initiatives, while restoring cuts to critical services ([nyc.gov](https://council.nyc.gov/julie-won/budget/)).
* In April 2024, the Public Housing Community Fund launched the "From Roots to Arts" program backed by a $3 million Mellon Foundation grant, funding artist residencies across five NYCHA campuses through 2026, including Astoria Houses in Queens ([citylimits.org](https://citylimits.org/new-program-seeks-nycha-artists-in-residence-to-help-beautify-public-housing-campuses/)).
* A February 2026 Center for an Urban Future report examined housing policies for artists in New York City, recommending zoning standards, artist-preference units, and set-asides to help secure workspace and housing ([policycommons.net](https://policycommons.net/artifacts/42939514/integrating-artists-into-nycs-affordable-housing-strategy/43838566/)).
* In November 2025, New York City lawmakers introduced a bill to allow certain housing programs to give preferences to working artists without conflicting with city fair-housing laws regarding occupational discrimination ([urgentmatter.press](https://www.urgentmatter.press/housing-programs-could-give-preference-to-artists-under-nyc-council-bill/)).

args.task: Check news or council releases in 2026 on the progress of the 'One Long Island City' planning study or District 26 comprehensive planning efforts.

result:
* The New York City Council and District 26 Council Member Julie Won unanimously approved the OneLIC Neighborhood Plan on November 12, 2025 ([nyc.gov](https://council.nyc.gov/julie-won/one-lic/)).
* The 54-block rezoning across Hunters Point and Dutch Kills is projected to yield 14,700 new housing units, including approximately 4,350 permanently affordable units through Mandatory Inclusionary Housing ([akerman.com](https://www.akerman.com/en/perspectives/new-york-city-council-approves-the-long-island-city-neighborhood-plan.html)).
* The plan incorporates nearly $2 billion in city commitments for capital investments, including funding for 1,300 new school seats and $206 million toward infrastructure improvements at the Queensbridge Houses ([nyc.gov](https://council.nyc.gov/julie-won/one-lic/)).
* Following the approval, the Pratt Center announced the facilitation of a "OneLIC Oversight Task Force" to monitor agency accountability and the timely delivery of these capital commitments ([prattcenter.net](https://prattcenter.net/our_work/onelic)).
* Projected timelines under the approved agreement scheduled the selection of a design consultant for waterfront elements to take place by June 2026 ([nyc.gov](https://council.nyc.gov/julie-won/one-lic/)).
* Subsequent design, permitting, and bidding for the waterfront and open space projects are scheduled to begin by June 2028, with construction targeted for completion by 2033 ([nyc.gov](https://council.nyc.gov/julie-won/one-lic/)).
